features.name: Academic credentials
features.description: Captures the level of formal relevant academic preparation or degree attainment presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience only, with no advanced degree presented.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field is presented.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related field is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures hands-on design or ownership of agent-based systems, especially their architecture, control boundaries, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as shown through concrete engineering problem solving or system improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms.
Gives a specific example of choosing a better structure or redesigning logic algorithmically.
Gives a strong example showing substantial performance, scalability, or tractability improvement from algorithmic skill.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures real experience shipping AI-enabled systems in production and understanding the reliability, evaluation, or guardrail work needed to operate them responsibly.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as serving developers and other internal users through usable defaults, low-friction tooling, and collaborative support.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, quantities, or named outcomes rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's real production engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter clearly states the results, effects, or operational consequences of the applicant's work rather than only naming activities.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists duties or technologies with little sense of outcome.
Implies positive effect, but without a clear result.
States a clear before-and-after outcome for at least one contribution.
Shows vivid or quantified operational impact that explains what changed for the team.

features.name: Narrative coherence and voice
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a memorable, coherent, well-shaped story or thesis rather than a generic or checklist-like summary.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented or offensive-security practice outside ordinary product work, such as CTF participation.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures contribution, upstream repair, or maintainer responsibility in public codebases used beyond the applicant's immediate employer or team.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, seriousness, and self-directed initiative shown through side projects or personal engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational or platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, services, or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the amount, breadth, and ownership of hands-on experience building, launching, maintaining, or operating real production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Programming language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the applicant presents beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and credibly the letter shows Python as a real production language for services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Requirement mapping
features.description: Captures how explicitly the letter maps the applicant's background to the specific qualifications, responsibilities, or requirements in the posting.

levels.descriptor: Makes little direct connection to the posting beyond naming the role.
Mentions some relevant qualifications, but the mapping to the posting is mostly implicit.
Clearly addresses several core requirements or responsibilities from the posting.
Systematically maps experience to the posting, with explicit coverage of the main requirements and responsibilities.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how clearly and compellingly the letter explains why this exact role is a particularly appealing next step for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues through activities like threat modeling, review, analysis, and remediation follow-through.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role as scaling security expertise and workflows through automation rather than treating it as generic software work.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credentials
features.description: Captures the presence, rigor, and relevance of formal external security certifications or credentials.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering rigor
features.description: Captures whether the letter conveys a serious philosophy of security-sensitive engineering emphasizing correctness, reliability, maintainability, careful boundaries, and long-term ownership.

levels.descriptor: Gives no clear signal of a personal engineering ethic around security-critical systems.
Implies care or correctness, but only indirectly.
States a clear philosophy of rigor, resilience, or seriousness about security work.
Conveys a distinctive and convincing personal ethic about holding security-sensitive systems to a higher standard.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability-report intake, triage, classification, routing, deduplication, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability handling automation is mentioned.
Security automation is mentioned, but the triage workflow itself remains vague.
The letter clearly shows experience automating vulnerability intake, routing, or triage.
The letter describes a high-resolution triage pipeline with elements like classification, deduplication, prioritization, ownership, or clear manual-work reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures surface-level mechanical quality of the letter, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and sentence-level professionalism.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures dimensions that are meaningfully evaluative but do not clearly belong to any larger recurring construct in this set.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not discuss the developers or teams who will use the tooling.
The letter shows a general desire to help teams, but not much detail about workflow impact.
The letter explicitly focuses on removing friction and making the secure path easier for engineers.
The letter consistently centers adoption, workflow fit, and secure-by-default behavior for busy developer teams.
